School y has a low value ($62) but high priority (rank 1). School z has a moderate value ($65) but low priority (rank 2).

Because most students favor y > x > w > z, y and x will likely be very competitive. Given my low priority at x, it's unlikely I will secure a match there unless many higher-priority students are unavailable or don't rank x highly. School w is likely to have fewer applicants due to its lower general preference, and my high priority there makes it a strong candidate for a stable match. School y, while having a low value for *me*, is highly desired by others and I have a high priority.

My strategy is to rank the schools based on a combination of my value and my priority, accounting for the likely competition. I will prioritize w as my first choice, as it offers a reasonable value and I am the highest priority applicant. I'll then rank x second, hoping to get in despite my lower priority, given its high value. Then y, as it is likely to have spots available due to high demand and my high priority. Finally, z as the least desirable option.

I believe this ranking will give me the best chance of securing a match at either w or x, and potentially y, while avoiding being stuck in a long deferral process hoping for x.
